:::{#thm-mgf-sum}
#### Moment generating function of a sum of independent random variables

If $X$ and $Y$ are [independent](independence.qmd#def-indpt),
and $M_X(t)$ and $M_Y(t)$ are defined at a number $t$, then:

$$M_{X+Y}(t) = M_X(t)\,M_Y(t)$$

:::

::: proof

[Functions](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/functions.html#def-function) of
[independent](independence.qmd#def-indpt) variables are independent,
so $\ef{tX}$ and $\ef{tY}$ are independent.
[Independent variables $A$ and $B$ satisfy $\E{AB} = \E{A}\,\E{B}$](variance-covariance.qmd#thm-indpt-uncorrelated),
so:

$$
\ba
M_{X+Y}(t)
&= \E{\ef{t(X+Y)}}
&& \text{(definition of the moment generating function)} \\
&= \E{\ef{tX}\,\ef{tY}}
&& \text{(} \ef{a+b} = \ef{a}\,\ef{b} \text{)} \\
&= \E{\ef{tX}}\,\E{\ef{tY}}
&& \text{(expectation of a product of independent variables)} \\
&= M_X(t)\,M_Y(t)
&& \text{(definition of the moment generating function)}
\ea
$$

:::
